symptom: Correct domain credentials rejected after five failed authentication attempts.
cause: The configured account-lockout threshold was reached.
resolution: Verified the test identity and account state, unlocked it01, then authenticated with the correct credential.
verification: LockedOut changed from true to false and Windows network logon returned success.
client_guidance: Stop retrying old passwords and ask the help desk for verified assistance.

symptom: The requester could not authenticate with the old credential.
cause: The submitted credential no longer matched the account password.
resolution: Reset to a unique temporary credential with change required, then completed an authenticated user password change.
verification: Old credential failed, NetUserChangePassword returned zero and the replacement credential authenticated successfully.
client_guidance: Request a verified reset and keep passwords out of support tickets.

symptom: Domain authentication failed for an otherwise correct credential.
cause: The test account was disabled.
resolution: Checked the approved lab account state and enabled finance01.
verification: Disabled account authentication failed; after enabling, the same credential succeeded.
client_guidance: Disabled accounts require an account-lifecycle review by the help desk.

symptom: Domain authentication failed after the account expiration date.
cause: The lab account expiration was in the past.
resolution: Reviewed expiration and cleared it for this permanent test account.
verification: Expired account rejected authentication; cleared expiration and successful network logon confirmed recovery.
client_guidance: Provide the relevant access authorization when requesting an account extension.

symptom: Local namespace authentication failed with error 1326.
cause: No local operations01 account exists.
resolution: Used CORP domain credentials.
verification: Windows LogonUser succeeded and token identity was CORP\operations01.
client_guidance: Use the domain username format supplied during onboarding.

symptom: Internal names failed with client DNS set to 10.77.0.99.
cause: Incorrect adapter DNS server.
resolution: Reset DNS to the DHCP-provided DC01 address and cleared the cache.
verification: DC01 resolved to 10.77.0.10 after repair.
client_guidance: Leave managed DNS automatic.

symptom: Helpdesk hostname resolved to unused 10.77.0.99.
cause: The application A record was incorrect.
resolution: Restored only helpdesk to 10.77.0.30 and cleared the client cache.
verification: Client resolution returned .30 and certificate-validated HTTPS returned 200.
client_guidance: Report the exact application hostname when requesting help.

symptom: Application resolution used .99 while authoritative DNS returned .30.
cause: An injected hosts-file override took precedence.
resolution: Restored the exact original hosts-file bytes and cleared DNS cache.
verification: Application resolution returned .30 and HTTPS port connectivity succeeded.
client_guidance: Do not add local hosts overrides for managed services.

symptom: A cache-only DNS lookup retained name-not-found after the authoritative record was created. Ordinary application lookups had refreshed automatically in earlier attempts.
cause: The cache-only query used a stale negative entry. A persistent outage in ordinary lookups was not reproduced on this Windows build.
resolution: Confirmed the record on DC01, cleared the client cache, then performed a fresh lookup.
verification: Fresh application resolution and a subsequent cache-only lookup both returned .30; the temporary record was removed. The fault was limited to cache-only retrieval.
client_guidance: Ask support to compare authoritative, fresh and cache-only results before refreshing cached DNS.

symptom: nslookup of FS01 failed while the FQDN resolved.
cause: The suffix search list had been changed to invalid.test.
resolution: Restored the saved suffix search configuration.
verification: nslookup expanded FS01 to FS01.corp.example.test and returned .20.
client_guidance: Provide the full server name when short names fail.

symptom: PC01 had a 169.254/16 APIPA address.
cause: The VM was attached to an empty internal switch without DHCP.
resolution: Reattached only PC01 to HelpDeskLab and renewed its lease.
verification: The client received a 10.77.0.0/24 DHCP address again.
client_guidance: Report a 169.254 address to support; do not invent a static address.

symptom: DC01 became unreachable after applying a /30 mask to an out-of-pool .250 client address.
cause: The client subnet mask was incorrect.
resolution: Removed the temporary manual address and restored DHCP and automatic DNS.
verification: DC TCP389 succeeded with a DHCP /24 address.
client_guidance: Keep managed IP settings automatic.

symptom: Client networking failed with its Ethernet adapter disabled.
cause: The lab adapter was disabled.
resolution: Enabled the same adapter and renewed DHCP.
verification: Adapter status was Up and FS01 TCP445 succeeded.
client_guidance: Report disabled adapters; avoid changing other network devices.

symptom: FS01 DNS resolved while TCP445 was blocked.
cause: The named Lab-T14 outbound rule blocked SMB.
resolution: Removed only the injected Lab-T14 rule.
verification: FS01 TCP445 succeeded and the temporary rule was absent.
client_guidance: Give support the server and service affected by a connection failure.

symptom: Internal SMB worked while external HTTPS connectivity failed.
cause: The client gateway was changed to unused .254.
resolution: Restored DHCP routing through HD01 at .1.
verification: The same external TCP443 probe succeeded again.
client_guidance: Keep the managed gateway configuration automatic.

symptom: hr04 was denied access to HR.
cause: The authorized user was missing from GG_HR.
resolution: Restored only hr04 membership in GG_HR.
verification: Fresh ordinary-user logon read, wrote and deleted successfully; another department remained denied.
client_guidance: Request approved department access; administrators should change only the missing permission.

symptom: finance04 was denied access to Finance.
cause: The department NTFS Allow rule was removed while SMB Change remained.
resolution: Restored the exact saved directory security descriptor.
verification: Fresh ordinary-user logon read, wrote and deleted successfully; another department remained denied.
client_guidance: Request approved department access; administrators should change only the missing permission.

symptom: sales04 was denied access to Sales.
cause: SMB Change was removed while the NTFS Modify grant remained.
resolution: Restored SMB Change for CORP\DL_Sales_Modify; confirmed NTFS was unchanged.
verification: Fresh ordinary-user logon read, wrote and deleted successfully; another department remained denied.
client_guidance: Request approved department access; administrators should change only the missing permission.

symptom: An existing user token remained denied after department membership was restored.
cause: The old logon and SMB session retained the earlier group authorization state.
resolution: Started a fresh Windows logon after restoring authorized membership.
verification: The retained token stayed denied and a new ordinary-user logon read, wrote and deleted in Operations.
client_guidance: Sign out completely and sign back in after an approved access change.

symptom: it04 could read Public but received Access Denied when writing.
cause: Public intentionally grants read-only access.
resolution: Confirmed the intended ACL and directed the requester to the writable IT department share.
verification: Public file read succeeded and write failed; the same ordinary user read, wrote and deleted in IT. No broad permission grant was made.
client_guidance: Use your department share to save work; Public documents are read-only.
